summary: Built the required node2/node3-via-node1 private-network topology (node1 eth1↔node2 10.10.12.0/24, node1 eth2↔node3 10.10.13.0/24) and applied a VyOS QoS rate-control policy (1mbit TBF) as an egress shaper on node1's eth2 interface, capping only node2→node3 traffic at 1 Mbit/s while leaving node3→node2 traffic unrestricted. Verified with real cross-node transfers (~0.96 Mbit/s node2→node3 vs ~4.6 Gbit/s node3→node2). All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (VyOS reconfiguration saved to config.boot, RHEL7 ifcfg/route files persisted), each proven via changed boot_id and confirmed to recover full connectivity and the shaping config after restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (VyOS)/node2/node3 (RHEL7) interfaces and found eth1/eth2 unconfigured, requiring topology setup
Configured node1 eth1 (10.10.12.1/24) and eth2 (10.10.13.1/24) via VyOS configure/commit/save
Configured node2 eth1 (10.10.12.2/24) and node3 eth1 (10.10.13.2/24) via persistent ifcfg files, plus static routes to each other's subnet via node1
Located VyOS qos policy rate-control and qos interface egress schema via on-node template files (no web access used per task restriction)
Applied `set qos policy rate-control LIMIT-TO-NODE3 bandwidth 1mbit` and `set qos interface eth2 egress LIMIT-TO-NODE3` on node1, committed and saved
Verified via tc that eth2 has a 1Mbit TBF root qdisc
Opened firewalld port 8000 temporarily on node2/node3 to run HTTP test servers, measured node2->node3 throughput (~0.96 Mbit/s, capped) and node3->node2 throughput (~4.6 Gbit/s, unrestricted)
Cleaned up test servers, test files, and firewall port rules on node2/node3
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node2 via `sudo reboot`, confirmed connection loss, polled until back, confirmed changed boot_id and recovered eth1 config/route/connectivity
Restarted node3 via `sudo reboot`, confirmed connection loss, polled until back, confirmed changed boot_id and recovered eth1 config/route/connectivity
Restarted node1 via `sudo reboot now`, confirmed connection loss/reset, polled until back, confirmed changed boot_id and that eth1/eth2 addresses and the 1Mbit TBF qdisc on eth2 persisted
Re-verified end-to-end ping connectivity in both directions after all three restarts

evidence.summary: VyOS qos policy rate-control (1mbit) applied as egress shaper on node1 eth2 (toward node3); tc qdisc confirms tbf rate 1Mbit; actual node2->node3 HTTP transfer measured at ~119866 bytes/s (~0.96 Mbit/s)
node3->node2 HTTP transfer measured at ~582,866,036 bytes/s (~4.6 Gbit/s), no shaping applied to that path (only egress on eth2 toward node3 was shaped)

evidence.requirement: Private-network topology: node2 and node3 communicate only through node1
evidence.summary: Configured node1 eth1 (10.10.12.1/24)/eth2 (10.10.13.1/24), node2 eth1 (10.10.12.2/24), node3 eth1 (10.10.13.2/24), and static routes on node2/node3 pointing to each other's subnet via node1; verified reachability via ping

evidence.summary: Post-restart bidirectional ping between node2 (10.10.12.2) and node3 (10.10.13.2) succeeded with 0% packet loss, confirming the shaped topology is fully functional after sequential node restarts
